newsitem.title: INDIA: Bomb in Indian sleeper train kills at least 12.
newsitem.headline: Bomb in Indian sleeper train kills at least 12.

text.p: A bomb exploded in a sleeper compartment in a train in northern India early on Monday, killing at least 12 passengers and injuring 37, police said.

The blast and ensuing fire destroyed two sleeper carriages just after the train pulled into Ambala cantonment near Chandigarh, capital of the northern state of Punjab, railway manager R.S. Grover told Reuters.
"It was a powerful bomb planted in one of the bogies (carriages)," Ambala police chief Rajbir Deswal told Reuters in Chandigarh. There were no immediate claims of responsibility.
A police spokesman said 14 of the passengers were seriously injured, and several of them might not survive.
United News of India (UNI) said the 1077 Jhelum Express was coming from the western city of Pune and was heading towards Jammu, winter capital of the troubled northern state of Jammu and Kashmir.

Grover said the explosion occurred at 3.07 a.m. (2137 GMT Sunday), some two minutes after the train pulled into the Ambala station, an important railway junction in northern India about 40 km (25 miles) south of Chandigarh.

State government officials in Jammu and Kashmir said the blast ripped through a second class sleeper carriage near the end of the train, which among its passengers was carrying some Hindu pilgrims to Jammu.
Police said the injured had been rushed to civil, military and railway hospitals.
The Press Trust of India said the death toll was expected to rise as several passengers were believed to have been trapped in one of the compartments which caught fire.
Railway officials said the damaged carriages were later separated from the train, which left Ambala for Jammu, where it was expected to arrive later in the morning.
In the 1980s, Punjab state was torn by a Sikh separatist rebellion in which at least 20,000 people died.
UNI said a senior leader of a splinter group of the regional Akali Dal party was gunned down on Sunday night.
It said Bichhitar Singh, a former state legislator from the Akali Dal (Badal) faction, was ambushed by four gunmen who opened fire on the jeep he was travelling in Ropar district of Punjab.
The Akali Dal is the political arm of many Sikhs who oppose separatist violence in the state, sometimes called India's food basket. Separatist militancy has largely died down in Punjab.

Jammu and Kashmir state, which neighbours Punjab, has been rocked by a separatist Moslem rebellion which militants launched in 1990. Police and hospital officials estimate that more than 20,000 people have died in the Kashmir revolt.
